$comment: Field table shown in step 4, in this order. placements: subset of off|front|back|on|word. 'side': learning = describes the learned word (always moved to the back of reverse cards); known = in the user's language; concept = language-neutral. 'langs': learning languages for which the row is shown ('*' = all active). 'modes': bilingual|same. Defaults may differ per learning language via 'defaultByLang'. 'more': the row is under "More…", closed by default.

fields.label: Word
fields.help: The word you are learning. Always on the question side of forward cards.

fields.label: Translation
fields.help: The word in your language, with a short hint when your language uses one word for several meanings. In same-language mode this is a short definition.

fields.label: Gender / article
fields.help: Shows the article (der Tisch, la mesa) or a gender mark (m/f/n) next to the word.

fields.label: Stress marks
fields.help: Marks the stressed vowel (молоко́). Applies to the word, its forms and the highlighted word in examples.

fields.label: Vowel marks
fields.help: The short-vowel signs (harakat) over and under the letters: كِتَاب rather than كتاب. Applies to the word, its forms and the highlighted word in examples.

fields.label: Reading (furigana)
fields.help: Kana reading above the kanji. Also controls furigana in example sentences.

fields.label: Romanization
fields.help: The word in Latin letters: Hepburn (Japanese), pinyin (Chinese), Revised Romanization (Korean), ALA-LC (Arabic), transliteration (Russian, Ukrainian, Armenian, Greek). For Chinese it also controls pinyin in example sentences.

fields.label: Other script
fields.help: Shows the word in the other Serbian script (Latin if the deck uses Cyrillic, and vice versa).

fields.label: Measure word / counter
fields.help: The classifier used when counting this noun (一本书, 鉛筆を三本, ba con mèo).

fields.label: Hanja
fields.help: Chinese characters behind Sino-Korean words (은행 → 銀行). Shown only for words that have them.

fields.label: Key forms
fields.help: The few forms you need to use the word: plural, genitive, past tense, aspect partner, verb class… not full tables.

fields.label: IPA
fields.help: Pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet.

fields.label: Examples
fields.help: Example sentences with the word highlighted. Use the slider to choose how many (0–3).

fields.label: Example translations
fields.help: Shows each example in your language when a matching translation exists. Some examples are written natively and have no translation.

fields.label: Antonyms & related
fields.help: Opposites and closely related words, in the language you are learning.

fields.label: Register
fields.help: Marks informal, formal, vulgar or offensive words.

fields.label: Emoji
fields.help: A picture hint for concrete words (💧 water). Most abstract words have none.

fields.label: Concept ID
fields.help: A tiny code at the bottom of the card (e.g. word-water). If you find a mistake while studying in Anki, include this code in your report so we can find the exact entry.

deckOptions.label: Reverse cards
deckOptions.help: Adds a second card per word: your language → the language you learn. On reverse cards everything about the learned word moves to the answer side so nothing gives the answer away.

deckOptions.label: Type the answer
deckOptions.help: On reverse cards you type the word instead of just recalling it. Anki compares your spelling with the main form (articles included, stress and vowel marks ignored).

deckOptions.label: Serbian script
deckOptions.help: Serbian is written in both Cyrillic and Latin. Choose the one used on your cards.
